author: estebanreyl
body:
**Purpose of the PR**
The primary goal of this PR is to optimize the purge process by introducing a new pool mechanism to the fetch portion of purge which today is one of the main limiting factors.  In a registry with a lot of OCI artifacts or indexes the current purge requires a manifest fetch for every single one. If these are done sequentially the probability of this taking too long is quite high. Instead, we introduce a pool mechanism that allows us to fetch multiple manifests concurrently.

***Changelog***
- Optimized fetch path by adding concurrency to manifest fetching
- Properly support nested indexes (Nested indexes should not get cleaned up if their parent is still in use)
- Added support for OCI index referrers
- Refactored the purge flow for increased readability. 
- Removed the separate dry run scenario and integrated this into the code 
- Changed existing pool mechanisms to use pond https://github.com/alitto/pond

***Validations***
- Unit tests have been added to account for new scenarios above, other unit tests have been updated to account for the change.
- Ran validations against real registries with the following configurations with a before and after time:

### Performance Improvements to Scanning
Most of the changes in this PR are optimizing the scanning of repositories, specifically for oci index and oci artifact scenarios as well as those involving child manifests. I ran some validation to fully cleanup a mix of distinct repos with 5000 untagged manifests and 200 untagged manifests each using dry-run (to avoid actually deleting) and --concurrency of 16 and observed the following performance improvements:

| Manifest Mix   | Old Binary (s) | New Binary (s) | % Change (A larger negative value is better)  |
|----------------|----------------|----------------|----------|
| 100% Docker | 58 | 55 | -5.17 |
| 100% OCI | 737 | 68 | -90.77 |
| 100% Lists | 72| 72 | 0.00 |
| 100% Indexes | 433 | 73 | -83.14 |
| Equal Split | 730 | 73 | -90.00 |

As can be observed there is no major change for registries using just docker manifests, however when we are dealing mith a mix of manifest types or oci indexes and oci manifests the performance improvement is pretty substantial

### Performance Comparison Matrixes When Actually carrying out deletes
The fixes in this PR are only substantial for situations that require substantial cleanup of larger registries. Purge itself seems to be rather hard to time as the actual delete times can have a large influence on the result but most of the changes are to the acquisition pathway. Nonetheless, to evaluate if there is otherwise any performance degradation, I ran the following scenarios and there seems to still be an overall improvement though I had some issues with the initial generation scripts so Ill update these numbers as those run for the larger repository scenarios. It might also be a good idea to bring such integration scenarios to the repo in the future but that is beyond the scope of this already large PR.

### Small Scale (50 Tags + 100 Untagged)

| Manifest Mix   | Old Binary (s) | New Binary (s) | Change   |
|----------------|----------------|----------------|----------|
| 100% Docker    | 39             | 36             | -7.69%   |
| 100% OCI       | 48             | 46             | -4.17%   |
| 100% Lists     | 42             | 45             | 7.14%    |
| 100% Indexes   | 31             | 29             | -6.45%   |
| Balanced       | 31             | 30             | -3.23%   |
| OCI Heavy      | 37             | 35             | -5.41%   |
| Equal Split    | 40             | 31             | -22.50%  |

### Scenario: 400 Tagged / 2000 Untagged
### Scenario: 500 Tagged / 4000 Untagged
### Scenario: 600 Tagged / 8000 Untagged

author: joctee
body:
This adds support for the Namron 8 button switches [4512772](https://efobasen.efo.no/produkter/vis/4512772) and [4512773](https://efobasen.efo.no/produkter/vis/4512773)

I have successfully tested that this works for `4512773`.

The reason for the new block in `button_maps.json` is that:

The **dim up** buttons (1,3,4,5) send these commands:
When holding down: MOVE_WITH_ON_OFF (0x05)
When releasing: STOP_WITH_ON_OFF (0x07)

The **dim down** buttons (2,4,6,8) send these commands:
When holding down: MOVE (0x01)
When releasing: STOP (0x03)

What I don't know is if `4512772` (or other devices) also need to use the new block in `button_maps.json` or not.
(I only own the 4512773)

The capitalization of the manufacturer should be all-caps for both `4512772` and `4512773`, but not for the other Namron devices.

This is a fork of #7615 . See the discussion in that PR for more details.

author: bruxy
body:
This commit addresses several aspects of JavaScript code quality within index.html to make it more professional, readable, and maintainable:

- Variable Naming: Renamed cryptic variable names (e.g., `c`, `j`, `d`) to more descriptive names (e.g., `mandelbrotCanvas`, `juliaCanvas`, `coordinatesDisplay`).
- Modernized Declarations: Replaced all `var` declarations with `let` or `const` as appropriate for block scoping and immutability.
- Code Comments: Added JSDoc-style comments to all functions, explaining their purpose, parameters, and return values. Added inline comments for complex logic sections, particularly within the fractal calculation loops and event handlers.
- Global Variables: Grouped related global variables into objects (e.g., `mandelbrotScope`, `juliaScope`, `appSettings`, `uiState`) to reduce global namespace pollution and improve organization.
- Function Organization:
    - Extracted pixel color calculation logic from `mandelbrot` and `julia` functions into a new helper function `calculatePixelColor`.
    - Extracted zoom calculation logic from `zoomWheel` into a new helper function `applyZoom`.
    - Improved clarity of variable names within `julia` and `zoomWheel`.

All changes were made directly within the `<script>` tag in `index.html` as per your requirements. Functionality of fractal generation, mouse interactions (movement for Julia seed, click to set seed), wheel zoom, and 'r' key reset have been maintained.

author: cbehn1
body:
This PR follows on PR #99. It adds support for decoding flat files containing Blocks other than those with the Ethereum structure.

The PR adds to the `decoder` crate an `enum AnyBlock`, whose variants represent chains - and associated data of Blocks - for which `decoder` can parse .dbin files. One of the fields in a `DbinHeader` is the `content_type`, which relates the data in a .dbin file to the Protobuf definition with which it was built. The `enum ContentType` lists our currently supported content types and its `try_from` method goes through the actual values found in the dbin headers.

These `enum`s can be extended to add more chains and content types in the future.

Note: commit eb65032357154acc4eb8d1f0b609f300b83c99c5 co-authored by @pedrohba1

body: ## **Description** This PR removes design and tech debt by cleaning up unused icon assets and modernizing the SmartAccountUpdateSplash component implementation. **What is the reason for the change?** - The previous implementation in PR #15355 added new filled icon variants (SpeedometerFilled, SparkleFilled, PetrolPump) when existing icons could be used - The component was using the older Icon component instead of the modern AvatarIcon component - Unused SVG assets were taking up space in the codebase **What is the improvement/solution?** - Removed 3 unused SVG files and their corresponding imports/enum entries - Replaced Icon component with AvatarIcon component for better design consistency - Updated icon names to use existing variants: SpeedometerFilled → Speedometer, PetrolPump → Gas, SparkleFilled → Sparkle - Added proper theming support with useTheme hook - Improved component structure by converting ListItem from arrow function to proper function component ## **Related issues** Fixes: N/A ## **Manual testing steps** 1. Navigate to a confirmation flow that triggers the Smart Account Update Splash 2. Verify that all three list items display with correct icons (speedometer, gas pump, sparkle) 3. Confirm that icons use proper theming (primary color with muted background) 4. Test in both light and dark themes to ensure proper color application 5. Verify that icon functionality and accessibility remain unchanged ## **Screenshots/Recordings** ### **Before** - Used filled icon variants (SpeedometerFilled, SparkleFilled, PetrolPump) - Used basic Icon component without proper theming - Extra SVG files in codebase ### **After** - Uses standard icon variants (Speedometer, Gas, Sparkle) - Uses modern AvatarIcon component with proper theming - Cleaner codebase with removed unused assets ## **Pre-merge author checklist** - [x] I've followed [MetaMask Contributor Docs](https://github.com/MetaMask/contributor-docs) and [MetaMask Mobile Coding Standards](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/blob/main/.github/guidelines/CODING_GUIDELINES.md). - [x] I've completed the PR template to the best of my ability - [x] I've included tests if applicable - [x] I've documented my code using [JSDoc](https://jsdoc.app/) format if applicable - [x] I've applied the right labels on the PR (see [labeling guidelines](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/blob/main/.github/guidelines/LABELING_GUIDELINES.md)). # 채팅 UI 개선: 메시지 가시성 및 교차 레이아웃 구현

이 PR은 채팅 인터페이스의 가시성 문제를 해결하고 사용자와 AI 메시지 간의 교차 레이아웃을 구현합니다.

## 주요 변경사항

1. **메시지 교차 레이아웃 구현**
   - 사용자 메시지: 오른쪽 정렬, 파란색 배경의 말풍선 형태
   - AI 메시지: 왼쪽 정렬, 회색 배경의 말풍선 형태
   - 프로필 아이콘과 메시지 내용의 순서를 사용자/AI에 따라 반전

2. **채팅 컨테이너 가시성 개선**
   - 채팅 컨테이너에 적절한 패딩 추가
   - 메시지 내용에 둥근 모서리와 패딩 적용
   - 배경색 대비 개선으로 가독성 향상

3. **타이핑 인디케이터 스타일링 개선**
   - AI 응답 로딩 시 타이핑 인디케이터를 메시지 말풍선 안에 배치
   - 일관된 스타일링으로 사용자 경험 개선

## 구현 방식

- 기존 애니메이션 및 스크롤 동작 유지
- Tailwind CSS의 조건부 클래스 적용을 위한 `cn()` 유틸리티 활용
- 반응형 디자인을 위한 최대 너비 제한 적용
- 메시지 타임스탬프 포맷팅 개선

## 스크린샷

이 PR은 채팅 인터페이스를 WhatsApp/iMessage 스타일의 대화형 UI로 변경하여 사용자와 AI 간의 대화를 더 직관적으로 구분할 수 있도록 합니다.

author: matthabermehl
body:
This commit introduces the foundational structure for the AWS MCP Server.

Key features included:
- Dockerized Node.js Express server to expose AWS SDK functionalities.
- Dynamic loading of AWS tools from the `tools/` directory. Each tool is a JavaScript class representing specific AWS SDK commands.
- Automatic generation of HTTP POST endpoints for each tool (e.g., /tools/s3/ListBuckets).
- Refactored tool files to use AWS credentials from environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION).
- Basic Tool class and logger implementation.
- Comprehensive README.md with instructions for building, running, and using the server.
- package.json with ES6 module support and necessary dependencies.
- Dockerfile for building the server image, including a non-root user for security.
- .env.example and .gitignore files.

The server allows you to interact with various AWS services by making HTTP requests to the corresponding tool endpoints.

author: ysthakur
body:
This PR provides completions for `z` and `zi`. Nushell no longer uses external completers for internal commands since v0.103 ([release notes](https://www.nushell.sh/blog/2025-03-18-nushell_0_103_0.html#external-completers-are-no-longer-used-for-internal-commands-toc)), so people's old external Zoxide completers won't work anymore.

This completer uses the options `completion_algorithm: "prefix", positional: false`. `positional` was [deprecated in 0.104](https://www.nushell.sh/blog/2025-04-29-nushell_0_104_0.html#substring-match-algorithm-toc) in favor of `completion_algorithm: "substring"`. However, I chose not to use the `substring` algorithm because it won't work in older versions of Nushell. Also, this completer will probably end up being updated in a few Nushell releases anyway (some improvements to Nushell's completers are planned).

This completer also looks a little weird if you type in multiple arguments. If you type in `z /foo bar<TAB>`, all the completions you see will have everything up to and including the first `/foo` stripped. It's not great, but it's needed because custom completers in Nushell can't currently choose which span they want to replace. Without it, if your first result upon typing `z /foo bar<TAB>` were `/foo/bar`, hitting Enter would replace your command line with `z /foo /foo/bar`, which is incorrect.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/cKElGuomdJVl7IF1ywrOLO7cE.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/cKElGuomdJVl7IF1ywrOLO7cE?t=7)

author: xinrong-meng
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?
Avoid INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX in `split`/`rsplit` when ANSI mode is on

### Why are the changes needed?
Ensure pandas on Spark works well with ANSI mode on.
Part of https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-52169.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Yes. INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX no longer fails `split`/`rsplit` when ANSI mode is on


```py
>>> spark.conf.get("spark.sql.ansi.enabled")
'true'
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> pser = pd.Series(["hello-world", "short"])
>>> psser = ps.from_pandas(pser)
```

FROM
```py
>>> psser.str.split("-", n=1, expand=True)
25/05/28 14:52:10 ERROR Executor: Exception in task 10.0 in stage 2.0 (TID 15)  
org.apache.spark.SparkArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: [INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX] The index 1 is out of bounds. The array has 1 elements. Use the SQL function `get()` to tolerate accessing element at invalid index and return NULL instead. SQLSTATE: 22003
== DataFrame ==
"__getitem__" was called from
<stdin>:1
...
```
TO
```py
>>> psser.str.split("-", n=1, expand=True)
       0      1                                                                 
0  hello  world
1  short   None
```


### How was this patch tested?
Unit tests

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?
No

This pull request focuses on improving the app's theme consistency by replacing hardcoded colors with theme attributes. The changes enhance maintainability and ensure the app adapts better to different themes, such as light and dark modes.

### Theme consistency improvements:

* Replaced hardcoded background color `#FFFFFF` with `?android:attr/windowBackground` in `fragment_bookings.xml` to align with the system's default background.
* Updated text colors in `fragment_bookings.xml` to use theme attributes like `?android:attr/textColorPrimary` and `?android:attr/textColorSecondary` instead of hardcoded values (e.g., `#000000`, `#555555`, `#888888`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d391257a606d0668744703a3a4c135e0eff278f65ba1ce4fd81813dc48825177L17-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d391257a606d0668744703a3a4c135e0eff278f65ba1ce4fd81813dc48825177L38-R46) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d391257a606d0668744703a3a4c135e0eff278f65ba1ce4fd81813dc48825177L69-R69) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d391257a606d0668744703a3a4c135e0eff278f65ba1ce4fd81813dc48825177L83-R83)

* Updated `item_my_booking.xml` to replace hardcoded colors (e.g., `@android:color/white`, `#FBD1A2`) with theme attributes like `?attr/colorOnPrimary` and `?attr/colorSecondary`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-11411c2f86079a3c66e15003ca521fd151c4649c5ca67134a1dd07e4c5e81749L11-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-11411c2f86079a3c66e15003ca521fd151c4649c5ca67134a1dd07e4c5e81749L26-R26) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-11411c2f86079a3c66e15003ca521fd151c4649c5ca67134a1dd07e4c5e81749L40-R55) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-11411c2f86079a3c66e15003ca521fd151c4649c5ca67134a1dd07e4c5e81749L70-L78)

author: npaton
body:
Fixed race condition where Stage.end() would crash when called before stage initialization completed, causing null timerID to be passed to addTransitions(). This occurred under high load (10+ simultaneous players) and would end games prematurely.

Changes:
- Add null check for timerID before calling addTransitions()
- Graceful error handling with debug logging when timerID unavailable
- Maintain backward compatibility for normal operation

Fixes #595

author: sayaad
body:
Seperate type imports and class imports for typescript client bindings codegen

# Description of Changes

Currently the code generation works fine following the typescript client setup tutorial in the documentation if you select Typescript+SWC as the variant in the vite template menu 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b8b16d2-9dbc-4b0e-b35d-5d6623c6dc95)
However if you select typescript only, the bindings generated by spacetimedb will not be bundled correctly by vite. This is described in vite's documentation here:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0dc34d4-42a3-441b-a779-33af01ebc0f5)
The end result is a client side error of trying to import a type from a JS file:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d225f14-8a55-48fa-8b13-383e7f7497ae)

This fix separates the type imports from the class imports in the generated typescript code, turning:
```ts
import {
  AlgebraicType,
  AlgebraicValue,
  BinaryReader,
  BinaryWriter,
  CallReducerFlags,
  ConnectionId,
  DbConnectionBuilder,
  DbConnectionImpl,
  DbContext,
  ErrorContextInterface,
  Event,
  EventContextInterface,
  Identity,
  ProductType,
  ProductTypeElement,
  ReducerEventContextInterface,
  SubscriptionBuilderImpl,
  SubscriptionEventContextInterface,
  SumType,
  SumTypeVariant,
  TableCache,
  TimeDuration,
  Timestamp,
  deepEqual,
} from "@clockworklabs/spacetimedb-sdk";
```
into
```ts
import {
  AlgebraicType,
  AlgebraicValue,
  BinaryReader,
  BinaryWriter,
  ConnectionId,
  DbConnectionBuilder,
  DbConnectionImpl,
  Identity,
  ProductType,
  ProductTypeElement,
  SubscriptionBuilderImpl,
  SumType,
  SumTypeVariant,
  TableCache,
  TimeDuration,
  Timestamp,
  deepEqual,
} from "@clockworklabs/spacetimedb-sdk";
import type {
  CallReducerFlags,
  DbContext,
  ErrorContextInterface,
  Event,
  EventContextInterface,
  ReducerEventContextInterface,
  SubscriptionEventContextInterface,
} from "@clockworklabs/spacetimedb-sdk";
```
solving the problem.

## Relevant issues

https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/issues/3024
https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/issues/2661

5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

#### What type of PR is this?

There is a new version v0.61.0 of otelgrpc

the changelog calls out the following:

The deprecated UnaryServerInterceptor in go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/google.golang.org/grpc/otelgrpc is removed, use NewServerHandler instead. (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/pull/7115)

Our early warning CI job for dependencies (https://prow.k8s.io/?job=ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-dependencies), found this problem, logs are here:
https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-dependencies/1925889909025935360/build-log.txt

```
ERROR(linux/amd64): /home/prow/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/go.etcd.io/etcd/server/v3/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/grpc.go:70:68: undefined: otelgrpc.UnaryServerInterceptor
ERROR(linux/amd64): /home/prow/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/storagebackend/factory/etcd3.go:328:39: undefined: otelgrpc.UnaryClientInterceptor
ERROR(linux/amd64): /home/prow/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/cri-client/pkg/remote_image.go:75:39: undefined: otelgrpc.UnaryClientInterceptor
ERROR(linux/amd64): /home/prow/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/cri-client/pkg/remote_runtime.go:107:39: undefined: otelgrpc.UnaryClientInterceptor
```

Here in this PR, we update to the closest version before the break, namely v0.60.0 and fix the 3 locations where we use the API which was dropped.

There is a PR in progress in etcd as well - https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/20017

we add an entry in hack/unwanted-dependencies.json as well to not go beyond v0.60.0 of otelgrpc, until we have a etcd tag with the PR above

author: gorgonzolast
body:
This pull request introduces a new feature to display a dashboard for team popularity based on betting activity, including both total stake and the number of bets. The changes span the addition of a new HTML template, a new view function, and updates to the URL configuration and imports.

Closes #60 

### New Feature: Team Popularity Dashboard

* **HTML Template for Dashboard**:
  - Created a new template `team_popularity.html` to display team popularity and betting statistics using a responsive design with Tailwind CSS. The dashboard includes two sections: "Most Popular Teams by Total Stake" and "Teams with Most Bets."

* **New View Function**:
  - Added `team_popularity_dashboard` in `views.py` to calculate and render team popularity data. It uses `Sum` and `Count` annotations to aggregate total stakes and the number of bets for each team.

### Supporting Changes

* **URL Configuration**:
  - Added a new route `/dashboard/team-popularity/` in `urls.py` to serve the team popularity dashboard.

* **Updated Imports**:
  - Imported `Sum` and `Count` from `django.db.models` in `views.py` to support the new view's database queries.

author: linho1219
body:
Add the graphType as part of the key during data join.

Before: After a join it could be possible that existing plots were left behind and never undraw, check this comment for more details https://github.com/mauriciopoppe/function-plot/issues/329#issuecomment-2906834864

After: After a join, because the key contains more properties (combination of `[function to graph, graphType]`) the old datum would be considered unmatched so it'd get removed, then the new datum gets drawn as if it was new.

Fixes #344, #329

author: chadlwilson
body:
Also cleans up some unnecessary use of IOUtils.copy when there are more canonical approaches in modern JVM, and removes some misleading old deprecations from the package metadata stores.

A major change here is removing the TFS impl from the server launcher lib, and just leaving it inside the actual WAR file.

This doesn't seem to make any difference, and the jar unpacks fine, loads correctly and seems to work. I am not sure why it was packaged in both places before, but perhaps due to some quirks no longer relevant with the latest/final SDK version or current JVMs.

In practice I intend to remove TFS support at some point when I can find a way to do it gracefully, so low concern that this this breaks someone.

author: tokitaku
body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the backend, transitioning the focus from a "Hero" domain to a "User" and "Sales" domain. It includes new CRUD operations, schema definitions, database configurations, and API routes for managing users and sales data. Additionally, it removes unused code and updates the database structure.

### Key Changes:

#### CRUD Operations and Database Models:
* Replaced `Hero`-related CRUD functions with `User` and `Sales` CRUD operations in `backend/crud.py`. Added functions for retrieving, creating, and querying users and sales records.
* Updated models in `backend/models.py` to define `User` and `Sales` tables, replacing the `Hero` model.

#### API Routes:
* Added new API routes in `backend/main.py` for creating and retrieving users and sales. Includes endpoints for filtering sales by year and department.

#### Database Configuration:
* Updated `backend/database.py` to configure a new SQLite database (`sales_info.db`) and provide a session dependency for FastAPI.
* Removed the redundant session dependency function from `backend/dependencies.py`.

#### Schemas:
* Defined new Pydantic schemas in `backend/schemas.py` for `User` and `Sales` entities, including `Create` and `Read` variants.

#### Cleanup and Utilities:
* Removed `Hero`-related test cases in `backend/tests/test_crud.py`.
* Added a utility script `backend/sql_drop_table.py` for dropping database tables.

author: ypatil12
body:
**Motivation:**

Currently, there's a bug in the `SM` where if you loop through the burnable shares queue, you may not clear all due to swap and pop of an Enumerable Map. Furthermore, we also are constrained by a token transfer taking too much gas and blocking transfer out of funds. 

**Modifications:**

- Iterate backwards on `decreaseBurnOrRedistributableShares ` 
- Overloaded `decreaseBurnableShares` with a version to pass in an index. This function will escrow a single share (called by above too). Now, we do not need a max strategy per opSet requirement
- Unit tests for both `increaseBurnOrRedistributableShares` and `decreaseBurnOrRedistributableShares`
- Added the following introspection:
-- `getBurnOrRedistributableShares(operatorSet, slashId) returns (Strategy[] Strats, uint256[] shares)
-- `getBurnOrRedistributableShares(operatorSet, slashId, strategy) returns (shares)
-- `getBurnOrRedistributableCount(operaotrSet, slashed) returns (count)`

**Result:**

Correct code with unit tests

author: vilereaver41
body:
This commit introduces a comprehensive system for loading game data (enemies, items, skills, status effects) from CSV files into structured Python objects.

Key changes include:

- New Core Classes:
  - `Enemy`: Enhanced with detailed attributes.
  - `Item`: Base class for all items.
  - `Equipment`, `Weapon`, `Consumable`, `Material`: Subclasses of `Item` for specific item types.
  - `Skill`: Base class for abilities and spells.
  - `Ability`, `PassiveSkill`, `Spell`: Subclasses of `Skill`.
  - `StatusEffect`: Represents buffs and debuffs.

- Data Loaders:
  - Dedicated loader functions for each CSV file, responsible for parsing and instantiating the corresponding objects.
  - Loaders handle various CSV structures, skip headers/comments, and perform basic data normalization.

- GameDataManager:
  - A central class (`GameDataManager`) manages the loading of all data types.
  - It ensures that data is loaded in the correct order and resolves dependencies (e.g., linking enemy abilities/loot to actual Skill/Item objects).
  - Provides getter methods for easy access to loaded game data.

- Unit Tests:
  - Comprehensive unit tests have been added for each data loader and for the `GameDataManager`.
  - Tests utilize temporary CSV files to ensure self-containment and reliability.
  - Key aspects tested include correct object instantiation, attribute parsing, handling of CSV irregularities, and proper data linking.

Implemented CSV files:
- `Enemy's Sheet.csv`
- `Armor, Accesories, Shields.csv`
- `Potions, Consumables, Materials.csv`
- `Revised Weapon Sheet.csv`
- `Spells & Abilitys.csv`
- `Buffs & Debuffs.csv`

This provides a foundational data layer for further game development.

author: elv-serban
body:
Fix audio rescale in the main transcoding flow.

The general idea is to rescale the decoded audio frame before sending to the filter (and then to the encoder).
Initialize the audio buffer source filter using the desired encoder timebase, such that the filter expects the frames to be in the encoder timebase and process correctly.
No longer rescale audio packets before sending them to the packager, because they are now returned by the encoder in the correct timescale of the encoder.

I left the video transcoding flow unchanged and will come back with a separate PR for video.

body:
## 変更内容

GitHubリリースからダウンロードされるzipファイルの名前を、バージョン番号付きから固定名に変更しました。

現在は `omakase-sync-0.2.2.zip` のような名前になりますが、この変更で常に `omakase-sync.zip` という名前になります。

### 技術的な詳細

- `get_package_download_url()` メソッドを修正し、固定名「omakase-sync.zip」を最優先で探すようにしました
- 固定名が見つからない場合は、従来通り拡張子が `.zip` のファイルを探します（後方互換性のため）
- いずれも見つからない場合は GitHub の `zipball_url` を使用します（既存の挙動を維持）

### 使用方法

リリース時に「omakase-sync.zip」という名前でzipファイルをGitHubリリースにアップロードしてください。

### テスト結果

以下のケースでテスト済み：
- 固定名のファイルがある場合：正しく固定名のURLが返される
- 固定名がなくバージョン付きzipがある場合：バージョン付きURLが返される（後方互換）
- zipファイルがない場合：zipball_URLが返される
- APIレスポンスがない場合：空文字が返される

Fixes #11.

body:
This commit includes the initial conversion of the Solana trading bot from Python to Node.js/TypeScript.

Key changes:
- Initialized a Node.js/TypeScript project with necessary dependencies (@solana/web3.js, typescript).
- Copied IDLs, bot configurations, and relevant project files.
- Removed original Python source files and Python-specific project files.
- Converted core Solana interaction logic from Python (src/core/*) to TypeScript (src/core/*), including client, wallet, curve calculations, pubkey constants, and priority fee management.
- Based on your feedback, all gRPC and Geyser-related components (Geyser listeners, .proto files, gRPC generated code) have been excluded from this conversion.
- Converted RPC/log-based monitoring components (src/monitoring/*) to TypeScript, including BlockListener, LogsListener, and their event processors.
- Converted trading logic (src/trading/*) to TypeScript, including base trading classes, buyer, seller, and the main trader orchestration class.
- Created index.ts files for easier module imports in core, monitoring, and trading directories.

The project now has a foundational TypeScript structure for core Solana interactions, RPC/log-based event monitoring, and trading logic.

Further steps will involve converting utility functions, configuration loading, implementing tests, and setting up the bot runner.

The gRPC/Geyser functionality was intentionally skipped due to difficulties in the automated environment for gRPC code generation and your subsequent request to focus on RPC-based features.

- **New Features**
  - Introduced a TypeScript-based trading bot system for Solana, including modules for wallet management, blockchain client, bonding curve calculations, trading operations (buy/sell), event processing, and listeners for blocks and logs.
  - Added support for dynamic and fixed priority fee management, with plugins to estimate transaction fees based on network conditions.
  - Implemented event-driven trading via real-time listeners for new token events using WebSocket and log subscriptions.
  - Provided comprehensive configuration and modular structure for extensibility.

- **Bug Fixes**

- **Chores**
  - Migrated the codebase from Python to TypeScript, removing all Python scripts, utilities, and tests.
  - Removed Python-specific configuration files and dependencies.
  - Added TypeScript project configuration and package management files.

- **Tests**
  - Removed all Python-based test scripts.

author: bavshin-f5
body:
Prerequisite for the allocator-api work, but useful on its own.

* `nginx_sys::detail` could be another crate (`nginx-common`?), but there's just not enough code to split it now.
* no fancy `fmt::Debug` for `ngx_str_t`. Need to figure out how to override bindgen generated trait implementation without nuking Debug impls from most of the bindings. `Builder::no_debug()` does exactly that -- omits `Debug` on the `ngx_str_t` itself **and** on any structs that include `ngx_str_t` recursively.
* I attempted to implement precision and padding for `display_bytes`, but apparently precision requires a honest UTF-8 character width detection algorithm ([unicode-width](https://crates.io/crates/unicode-width)). The code without that can panic on an attempt to break an UTF-8 sequence. Maybe next time.
* Conversions and comparisons might be excessive. I took an inspiration from the [bstr](https://crates.io/crates/bstr) and left only types we realistically expect to use.
  I wish I could replace NgxStr with `bstr`, but it does not offer allocators support :(

author: fintelia
body:
I decided to look into improving compile times inspired by https://github.com/image-rs/image/issues/2244#issuecomment-2544563417

It turns out that a lot of time is spent compiling image format encoders for reasons that are somewhat subtle: Due to how the Rust compiler is implemented, methods with generic arguments get compiled when building a crate that uses them, while methods with concrete types get compiled when building the crate that defines them. 

In particular, the `save` family of methods in this crate take a generic argument (their "path" parameter) but were previously implemented to call a concrete `save_buffer_with_format_impl` version to handle the actual encoding / saving of the data. However at the same time, the various format crates that we depend on expose encoders that are themselves generic over the `std::io::Write` implementation that they output data to. That means that the actual concrete instantiation of the encoders would happen inside the _image_ crate, which is perhaps the worst time. It is too early to know whether downstream code actually needs encoding functionality, but too late to fully parallelize the compilation of different format encoders because in rustc (portions?) of crate compilation are sequential.

This PR shifts things around so that the encoders will get monomorphized in downstream code, but only if someone actually calls one of the `save` methods in their own code. On my machine it speeds up release build times by 3+ seconds.

---
Additionally this PR rewords the doc comments and moves the definitions of `save_buffer` and `save_buffer_with_format` to free_functions.rs where their implementations already were.

author: axke
body:
This feature adds a tooltip duration setting, a new notification mode, and shows the stock on hover of the toolbar message. As usual, feel free to reject or request updates.

### Relevant Suggestions
[Remove on Game Interaction](https://discord.com/channels/420803245758480405/1375212401615441930)
[Stock in Toolbar](https://discord.com/channels/420803245758480405/1372739011390738502)
[Audio Alert](https://discordapp.com/channels/420803245758480405/1379283217701666856)
[Special Worlds](https://discordapp.com/channels/420803245758480405/1376235290527793154)

### Stock in Toolbar
Adds stock as a title for the toolbar alert
- Stock is handled by the api sending to the alt1 daemon
  - Of note, this is on, so the api will need to be ready when this is merged in. It will gracefully fail, but still would be best for the api to be there
- The stock will update in the background, however, calls will still require the application to be open 

![{4EEFA941-D6F6-41EF-9752-4C6CDF0735F0}](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c6f7ce2-fca4-49fb-93e1-7962f126c2f2)

### Tooltip Duration Setting
Settings are as follows:
- Default (5s)
  - Keeps current 5s removal, will be the default mode
- 30s 
- 1m
- Interaction or expiration
  - If an interaction happens, it will clear as soon as the interaction happens with a minimum time of 2.5s. The maximum time it will show is the remaining duration. 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/594d89cc-5e11-4aea-9a9d-4190aa2e5616)

### System Notification
The new notification mode is called `System`...this name can be changed, but it made the most sense. It uses the alt1 notification system, which sends a Windows notification. 
- Seems like this requires Windows to allow notifications (which makes sense, so verbiage in the notifications info modal may need added)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e241047-946b-4819-8846-16d86c6c7e2d)

### Audio Notification
Adds a new notification mode called `Audio`. This will play the mp3 located at `alt1/assets/sounds/notification.mp3` if turned on. It will only play once.

![{5453451C-4E96-4A3C-9594-03EEF3933B15}](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f052e6f-4c8c-4bff-953b-1da8949da8fe)

### Abbreviated Calls
Added a call to allow the usage of the abbreviated called. Left the default to that as off.

### Special Worlds
Added special world icon to the toolbar notification and to the event grid.

![{EFE20014-87D5-4B09-ACD7-E177CBCD67B1}](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/003c707b-4e6b-4787-9316-ffeb0f3664bb)

### Settings Panel Overhaul
Updated settings to be in collapsible, grouped panels. This also led me to doing some minor style changes in this panel, primarily for consistency and readability.

![{377E56C5-4A3D-4531-8451-0A9A1BFC6852}](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/984b9de0-4f0f-4aa9-aa3f-18a9bd9a2860)
![{FFC75516-EECE-42D8-9A4C-20798779C396}](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c8a2c9f-39fa-4730-a1b9-d73b495c7dc6)

Light mode
![{364EF41B-6525-467B-B457-789E22612A6B}](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92e7687c-a42f-455b-8d75-5b278e6c7ed8)

### Webpack Change
The webpack was using an absolute path, so it wasn't running properly locally with the setup I use. I updated it to use a relative. I'm not sure if there are other implications at play here, so if that needs removed and I just need to set it when I develop, that's fine.

author: y16ra
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: loonghao
body:
## Problem

The vcpkg package creation process was failing with "Process completed with exit code 1" because it was trying to process both x64 and x86 architectures, but only x64 artifacts were available from the build process.

**Additionally, this issue revealed a critical gap in our PR testing**: PR tests were only testing `--type test` packages but not `--type vcpkg` packages, which allowed this issue to slip through to release.

## Root Cause

### 1. Architecture Handling Issue
The `copy_vcpkg_artifacts` function was hardcoded to expect both x64 and x86 architectures:

```bash
for arch in x64 x86; do
    # Process artifacts...
    if artifacts not found:
        return 1  # This caused the failure
done
```

When x86 artifacts were missing (which is normal for PR builds that only build x64), the function would fail and exit with code 1.

### 2. Test Coverage Gap
- **PR tests**: Only tested `--type test` (simplified test packages)
- **Release workflow**: Used `--type vcpkg` (full vcpkg packages)
- **Result**: Critical vcpkg packaging logic was never tested in PRs

## Solution

### 1. Dynamic Architecture Discovery
- Modified `copy_vcpkg_artifacts` to first discover what architectures are actually available
- Only process architectures that have corresponding artifact directories
- Improved logging to show which architectures were found

### 2. Flexible Directory Creation
- Updated `package_vcpkg` to only create directory structures for available architectures
- Prevents creation of empty architecture directories
- Maintains vcpkg compatibility while being more robust

### 3. Enhanced Header File Handling
- Modified `copy_header_files` to accept dynamic architecture lists
- Only copies headers to directories that actually exist
- Maintains backward compatibility with default behavior

### 4. **Comprehensive PR Testing** 🆕
- **Added actual vcpkg package creation test to PR workflow**
- Now tests both `--type test` AND `--type vcpkg` in PRs
- Prevents future regressions by testing the actual release packaging logic
- Ensures PR tests match release workflow behavior

## Changes Made

### `.github/scripts/unified-packaging.sh`

#### `package_vcpkg()` Function
- Added architecture discovery logic before creating directories
- Only creates directories for architectures with available artifacts
- Improved error handling and logging

#### `copy_vcpkg_artifacts()` Function
- Implemented two-phase approach: discovery then processing
- Added comprehensive logging for debugging
- Graceful handling of missing architectures
- Better error messages with available directory listings

#### `copy_header_files()` Function
- Updated to accept dynamic architecture list as parameters
- Maintains backward compatibility with default x64/x86 behavior
- Only processes architectures that have corresponding directories

### `.github/workflows/pr-build-test.yml` 🆕
- **Added vcpkg package creation test alongside existing test package creation**
- Prepares proper artifact directory structure for vcpkg packaging
- Tests both package types to ensure comprehensive coverage
- Now catches vcpkg packaging errors before they reach release

## Expected Results

After this fix:

✅ **Single Architecture Builds**: vcpkg packages can be created with only x64 artifacts
✅ **Multi Architecture Builds**: Still works when both x64 and x86 artifacts are available
✅ **Better Error Handling**: Clear error messages when no artifacts are found
✅ **Improved Logging**: Detailed information about discovered architectures
✅ **Robust Processing**: No more failures due to missing expected architectures
✅ **Comprehensive PR Testing**: Both test and vcpkg package creation are tested in PRs
✅ **Early Error Detection**: vcpkg packaging issues caught before release

## Testing

This fix should be tested by:
1. ✅ Running PR builds (which typically only build x64) to ensure vcpkg package creation succeeds
2. Running full release builds (with both x64 and x86) to ensure compatibility
3. Verifying that the created packages contain the correct architecture-specific files
4. Checking that error messages are helpful when no artifacts are found
5. ✅ **Confirming that PR tests now catch vcpkg packaging errors**

## Backward Compatibility

This change is fully backward compatible:
- When both x64 and x86 artifacts are available, behavior is identical to before
- When only one architecture is available, the package is created successfully instead of failing
- All existing vcpkg package consumers will continue to work unchanged
- PR testing is enhanced but doesn't break existing workflows

## Related Issues

Fixes:
1. The vcpkg package creation failure seen in CI where the process would exit with code 1 when trying to process missing x86 artifacts during PR builds
2. **The test coverage gap that allowed this issue to slip through to release**

## Lessons Learned

⚠️ **Important**: This issue highlighted that our PR tests were not comprehensive enough. The fix includes both the immediate problem AND the underlying test coverage issue to prevent similar problems in the future.

## Summary
Implements proper YAML front matter parsing and metadata extraction for markdown files, replacing the initial implementation that only removed front matter.

Closes #27

## Changes
- Added `python-frontmatter` dependency for robust YAML parsing
- Parse and extract metadata fields from YAML front matter:
  - `title`: Used as document title (takes precedence over generated titles)
  - `created_at`: Used for chunk creation timestamp
  - `updated_at`: Used for chunk modification timestamp  
  - `uri`: Stored in metadata JSON field
  - Other fields are preserved in metadata
- Updated `extract_content()` to return tuple of `(content, language, metadata)`
- Modified crawler to use metadata title when available
- Updated processor to use metadata dates for chunk timestamps
- Added comprehensive test coverage for various YAML front matter formats

## Implementation Details
The implementation follows this flow:
1. **Extractor**: Parses YAML front matter using `python-frontmatter`, extracts supported fields
2. **Crawler**: Merges extracted metadata with existing metadata, uses metadata title if available
3. **Processor**: Uses metadata dates for chunk timestamps, stores other metadata in JSON field
4. **Database**: Stores title, created_at, updated_at as columns; uri and other fields in metadata JSON

## Test Plan
- [x] Added 7 new test cases for YAML front matter parsing
- [x] Updated existing tests to handle new function signatures
- [x] All 113 tests pass
- [x] Linting passes (ruff)
- [x] Type checking passes (mypy)

## Example Usage
Markdown file with YAML front matter:
```markdown
---
title: My Document Title
created_at: 2024-01-01T10:00:00Z
updated_at: 2024-01-15T15:30:00Z
uri: https://example.com/docs/my-document
tags: [python, documentation]
---
# Document Content

This content will be indexed without the YAML front matter,
but the metadata will be properly stored and searchable.
```

author: graciofilipe
body:
I've made sure the "RatingDate" column is now consistently processed as a string throughout your application.

Changes include:
- I removed the explicit conversion of 'RatingDate' to datetime objects in `st_app.py` before writing to BigQuery.
- I updated the BigQuery schema in `st_app.py` to define 'RatingDate' as STRING instead of TIMESTAMP.
- I modified `test_handle_fetch_data_action_rating_date_conversion` in `test_st_app.py` to assert that 'RatingDate' maintains a string/object dtype in the DataFrame.
- I verified that `test_write_to_bigquery_with_selection_and_schema` correctly reflects 'RatingDate' as a string for BigQuery schema purposes.

This ensures that the original string representation of "RatingDate", as fetched from the API or other sources, is preserved, particularly when stored in BigQuery.

author: hk669
body:
This pull request introduces enhancements to the asset search functionality, including support for advanced operators, case-insensitive searches, improved handling of attributes, and integration with utility methods for result processing. The changes aim to make asset searches more flexible and user-friendly while maintaining robust error handling.

### Enhancements to Asset Search Functionality:
* **Support for advanced operators**: Added new operators like `contains`, `between`, and case-insensitive versions of existing operators (`startswith`, `eq`, `neq`) for more flexible search conditions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2ebcf39a0ee27cec003648a57941f0d11cbcc0db4bea36e84f26e68f5d76367eR154-R174) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2ebcf39a0ee27cec003648a57941f0d11cbcc0db4bea36e84f26e68f5d76367eR185-R218) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2ebcf39a0ee27cec003648a57941f0d11cbcc0db4bea36e84f26e68f5d76367eR247-R295) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2ebcf39a0ee27cec003648a57941f0d11cbcc0db4bea36e84f26e68f5d76367eL266-R390)
* **Default attributes inclusion**: Introduced `DEFAULT_SEARCH_ATTRIBUTES` to ensure essential attributes are included in search results by default, with support for additional user-specified attributes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2ebcf39a0ee27cec003648a57941f0d11cbcc0db4bea36e84f26e68f5d76367eL322-L344) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3c2e7532b2dde667ab920c436615a85018a54023f13a3906157d3c1c3674e409R1-R17)
* **Improved handling of `where_some` conditions**: Enhanced the handling of "some" conditions to support advanced operators and case-insensitive searches.

### Integration with Utility Methods:
* **Result processing**: Integrated `SearchUtils.process_results` for standardized post-processing of search responses, replacing direct handling of results. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-38aa390657481d4b7b6d0e02aff9ab560a6c8cd11fa63a287a1485253f7ff37aL49-R56) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2ebcf39a0ee27cec003648a57941f0d11cbcc0db4bea36e84f26e68f5d76367eL370-R516)
* **Utility imports**: Added imports for `SearchUtils` and constants to streamline search functionality. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-38aa390657481d4b7b6d0e02aff9ab560a6c8cd11fa63a287a1485253f7ff37aR7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2ebcf39a0ee27cec003648a57941f0d11cbcc0db4bea36e84f26e68f5d76367eR9-R10)

### Expanded Search Scenarios:
* **Search scenarios**: Added examples for searching assets with complex conditions, including case-insensitive matching, range filtering, and OR logic for multiple values. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ff695b73f10f2a8b20223a7fe7ddc34b6560080412603326f5e89aeffa57f3a9R111-R138) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ff695b73f10f2a8b20223a7fe7ddc34b6560080412603326f5e89aeffa57f3a9R186-R199)

Closes #77

author: baronvonbirra
body:
This commit introduces a significant overhaul of the website's user interface and user experience, along with several new features and improvements.

Key changes include:

- **Modernized Styling:** Implemented a new, modern theme with an updated color palette, typography (Inter and Poppins fonts), and spacing. Global styles and component-specific styles have been updated for a cohesive look and feel.
- **Enhanced Home Page:**
    - Redesigned the home page with a more welcoming layout.
    - Added a "Cocktail of the Week" feature to prominently display a selected cocktail.
- **Updated Category Display:** Category list items now include icons for specific categories (Rum and Whiskey), enhancing visual appeal.
- **Improved Cocktail Display:**
    - Cocktail list items now use a placeholder image if a specific cocktail image is unavailable.
    - The cocktail detail page (`CocktailDetail.jsx`) now displays new information fields from `cocktails.json`, including history, glass type, difficulty, tags, flavor profile, and tools needed.
- **Comprehensive Testing:**
    - Added new unit tests for `CategoryListItem.jsx` and `CocktailListItem.jsx`.
    - Updated and added tests for `HomePage.jsx` to cover the "Cocktail of the Week" feature.
    - Updated tests for `CocktailDetail.jsx` to cover the newly displayed fields.
    - Resolved all previous test failures related to theme provider setup, ensuring a stable test suite (24/24 tests passing).

These changes aim to provide a more engaging, informative, and visually appealing experience for you when interacting with the cocktail recipes.

author: zutousan
body:
This commit introduces a comprehensive set of C++ code examples demonstrating key features from C++11, C++14, C++17, and C++20.

Features include:
- C++11: auto, lambdas, range-for, nullptr, enum class, override/final, move semantics, initializer lists, std::thread, chrono, smart pointers, tuple, regex.
- C++14: Generic lambdas, binary literals, return type deduction, std::make_unique, std::shared_timed_mutex.
- C++17: Structured bindings, if constexpr, inline variables, nested namespaces, std::filesystem, optional, variant, any, parallel algorithms.
- C++20: Concepts, ranges, coroutines, three-way comparison, basic modules, std::format, std::span, std::latch.

Each feature is demonstrated in a small, self-contained .cpp file with explanations and compilation guidance. The examples are organized by C++ version and category (core language, standard library). A main README.md provides an overview and navigation for the project.

### [`v1.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/sbt/sbt/releases/tag/v1.11.0): 1.11.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/sbt/sbt/compare/v1.10.11...v1.11.0)

#### Central Repository publishing

The Central Repository (aka Maven Central) has long been the pillar of the JVM ecosystem including Scala. The mechanism to publish libraries to the Central has been hosted by Sonatype as OSS Repository Hosting (OSSRH) via HTTP PUT, but in March it was [announced](https://central.sonatype.org/news/20250326\_ossrh_sunset/) that the endpoint will be sunset in June 2025 in favor of the [Central Portal](https://central.sonatype.org/publish/publish-portal-guide/) at <https://central.sonatype.com/>.

sbt 1.11.0 implements a built-in support to publish to Central Repository via the Central Portal. To publish to the Central Portal, first set `ThisBuild / publishTo` setting to the `localStaging` repository:

```scala
ThisBuild / publishTo := {
  val centralSnapshots = "https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots/"
  if (isSnapshot.value) Some("central-snapshots" at centralSnapshots)
  else localStaging.value
}
```

Add `credentials` to the host `central.sonatype.com` using the generated user token user name and password. When you're ready to publish, call `publishSigned` task (available via [sbt-pgp](https://redirect.github.com/sbt/sbt-pgp)). At this point, the JARs and POM files will be staged to your local `target/sona-staging` directory.

Next, call `sonaUpload` to upload to the Central Portal and manually release the bundle, or call `sonaRelease` to upload and automatically release to the Central Repository.

This was contributed by [@​eed3si9n](https://redirect.github.com/eed3si9n) in [#​8126](https://redirect.github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8126). The feature was inspired by sbt-sonatype workflow pioneered by Taro Saito, and [sonatype-central-client](https://redirect.github.com/lumidion/sonatype-central-client) spearheaded by David Doyle at [Lumidion](https://www.lumidion.com/).

#### Other updates

-   fix: Avoid printing "copying runtime jar" etc to stdout by [@​eed3si9n](https://redirect.github.com/eed3si9n) in [https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8081](https://redirect.github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8081)
-   fix: Fix incremental test (`testQuick`) with companion objects by [@​eed3si9n](https://redirect.github.com/eed3si9n) in [https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8087](https://redirect.github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8087)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/sbt/sbt/compare/v1.10.11...v1.11.0

<details>
<summary>jawah/charset_normalizer (charset-normalizer)</summary>

### [`v3.4.7`](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#347-2026-04-02)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.6...3.4.7)

##### Changed

- Pre-built optimized version using mypy\[c] v1.20.
- Relax `setuptools` constraint to `setuptools>=68,<82.1`.

##### Fixed

- Correctly remove SIG remnant in utf-7 decoded string. ([#​718](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/718)) ([#​716](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/716))

### [`v3.4.6`](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#346-2026-03-15)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.5...3.4.6)

##### Changed

- Flattened the logic in `charset_normalizer.md` for higher performance. Removed `eligible(..)` and `feed(...)`
  in favor of `feed_info(...)`.
- Raised upper bound for mypy\[c] to 1.20, for our optimized version.
- Updated `UNICODE_RANGES_COMBINED` using Unicode blocks v17.

##### Fixed

- Edge case where noise difference between two candidates can be almost insignificant. ([#​672](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/672))
- CLI `--normalize` writing to wrong path when passing multiple files in. ([#​702](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/702))

##### Misc

- Freethreaded pre-built wheels now shipped in PyPI starting with 3.14t. ([#​616](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/616))

### [`v3.4.5`](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#345-2026-03-06)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.4...3.4.5)

##### Changed

- Update `setuptools` constraint to `setuptools>=68,<=82`.
- Raised upper bound of mypyc for the optional pre-built extension to v1.19.1

##### Fixed

- Add explicit link to lib math in our optimized build. ([#​692](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/692))
- Logger level not restored correctly for empty byte sequences. ([#​701](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/701))
- TypeError when passing bytearray to from\_bytes. ([#​703](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/703))

##### Misc

- Applied safe micro-optimizations in both our noise detector and language detector.
- Rewrote the `query_yes_no` function (inside CLI) to avoid using ambiguous licensed code.
- Added `cd.py` submodule into mypyc optional compilation to reduce further the performance impact.

### [`v3.4.4`](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#344-2025-10-13)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.3...3.4.4)

##### Changed

- Bound `setuptools` to a specific constraint `setuptools>=68,<=81`.
- Raised upper bound of mypyc for the optional pre-built extension to v1.18.2

##### Removed

- `setuptools-scm` as a build dependency.

##### Misc

- Enforced hashes in `dev-requirements.txt` and created `ci-requirements.txt` for security purposes.
- Additional pre-built wheels for riscv64, s390x, and armv7l architectures.
- Restore ` multiple.intoto.jsonl` in GitHub releases in addition to individual attestation file per wheel.

### [`v3.4.3`](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#343-2025-08-09)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.2...3.4.3)

- mypy(c) is no longer a required dependency at build time if `CHARSET_NORMALIZER_USE_MYPYC` isn't set to `1`. ([#​595](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/595)) ([#​583](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/583))

- Custom build backend to overcome inability to mark mypy as an optional dependency in the build phase.
- Support for Python 3.14

##### Fixed

- sdist archive contained useless directories.
- automatically fallback on valid UTF-16 or UTF-32 even if the md says it's noisy. ([#​633](https://redirect.github.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/633))

- SBOM are automatically published to the relevant GitHub release to comply with regulatory changes.

author: mladen5000
body:
This commit introduces a major refactoring of the StrainR codebase to improve quality, maintainability, and documentation.

Key changes include:

- **Code Restructuring:**
    - Implemented class-based workflows for core functionalities: - `DatabaseBuilder` in `bin/strainr-db.py` for database creation. - `KmerClassificationWorkflow` in `strainr/strainr-classify-clean.py` for k-mer based classification. - `PangenomeAnalysisWorkflow` in `strainr/strainr-pangenome.py` for pangenome analysis.
    - Refactored key modules into classes:
        - `KmerStrainDatabase` in `strainr/kmer_database.py` for managing k-mer data.
        - `ClassificationAnalyzer` in `strainr/analyze.py` for handling post-classification analysis steps (hit separation, disambiguation).
- **Code Quality:**
    - Added comprehensive type hints to functions, methods, and variables across most of the codebase.
    - Implemented Google Python Style docstrings for modules, classes, and functions.
    - Refactored variable and function names for clarity and adherence to Python conventions (snake_case, PascalCase).
    - Improved error handling and logging in several modules.
- **Testing:**
    - Added a comprehensive unit test suite for the `KmerStrainDatabase` class in `tests/test_kmer_database.py`.
- **Argument Parsing:**
    - Reviewed and enhanced command-line argument parsing for `strainr-db.py`, `strainr-classify-clean.py`, and `strainr-pangenome.py` for clarity and consistency.
- **Documentation:**
    - Updated `README.md` to reflect the new architecture and usage.
    - Overhauled the Sphinx documentation in `docs/`:
        - Updated `conf.py` to enable `autodoc` and `napoleon`.
        - Created a new documentation structure with individual pages for introduction, installation, usage, and API reference. - Added `.rst` stubs for API documentation generation. - The Sphinx build is partially successful; `strainr/output.py` (incomplete due to my own errors) causes `autodoc` failures for that specific module.
- **Dependency Management:**
    - Confirmed that `jellyfish` is not used, so no replacement was necessary.

**Note on `strainr/output.py`:**
Due to persistent errors I encountered during development, the refactoring of `strainr/output.py` (intended to house an `AbundanceCalculator` class) could not be completed. This file remains in an incomplete state. Abundance calculation logic was instead incorporated directly into the workflow classes (`KmerClassificationWorkflow`, `PangenomeAnalysisWorkflow`) for the time being.

author: kotiuksofiia
body:
*Problem:*
- Both `BudgetLimitRepository` and `TransactionRepository` duplicate the same Add/Update/Delete logic, each calling SaveChangesAsync() directly.
- Performing context changes in multiple repositories violates the DRY principle and makes maintenance more difficult.

*Solution:*
- Introduced a GenericRepository base class that implements core CRUD operations using the Template Method pattern.
- Refactored BudgetLimitRepository and TransactionRepository to inherit from GenericRepository, overriding only the methods that require eager loading (Include) or custom business logic.
- Registered the open generic IGenericRepository as well as the specific repository interfaces in the DI container.

*Benefits:*
- DRY: centralizes all CRUD logic in one place.
- SRP: each repository now contains only its domain‐specific behavior.
- OCP: changes to CRUD behavior can be made in the base class without modifying derived repositories.

author: zylaah
body:
This commit significantly enhances the download manager script by:

- Fixing the download progress display (bytes and percentage).
- Implementing text file snippet previews for common text-based formats.
- Making all file previews (image, text, generic icon) clickable to open the downloaded file with its default application.
- Improving image preview reliability by:
    - Adding a fallback to detect image types based on file extensions when `contentType` is missing.
    - Expanding supported image formats to include `.ico`, `.tif`, `.tiff`, and `.jfif`.
- Resolving a race condition where clicking a file preview during the AI renaming process could lead to "file not found" errors. The preview is now temporarily unclickable during renaming.
- Enhancing overall script robustness through improved download key generation, more reliable file/stream handling for previews, platform-agnostic path management, UI update throttling, and more detailed error/debug logging.

author: datapythonista
body:
Closes #383 

With these changes, it'll be possible to do things like this with pandas and blosc2:

```python
import pandas
import blosc2

def my_func(x):
    return np.sin(x * 2)

s = pandas.Series([1, 2, 3], index=list('abc'), name='sample')

# blosc2 will jit the function
print(s.map(my_func, engine=blosc2.jit))
```

In this PR I'm assuming that `blosc2.jit` is intended to be used with vectorized numpy operations. If that's not the case, and you want to support scalar functions and jit Python loops (see example below), let me know and we can implement this for map:

```python

@blosc2.jit
def my_func(array):
    for item in array:
        scalar_udf(item)
```

Also, `apply` is designed in pandas to call the udf for each column or row in a dataframe. I'm passing the whole array since it's a numpy array and I think operations should be vectorized, but I can make it work by columns or rows.

author: roy651
body:
Integrates Gradio into the `handwriting_recognition.ipynb` notebook to provide interactive demos:

1.  **Single Character Demo:**
    *   Allows you to draw a character on a sketchpad or upload an image.
    *   You can select between the trained `ImprovedCNN` or `VGG19` models.
    *   Displays the predicted character and confidence score.

2.  **Multiple Character Demo:**
    *   Allows you to upload an image of a word or sentence.
    *   Implements character segmentation using OpenCV (contour detection) to isolate individual characters.
    *   Feeds segmented characters to the selected model.
    *   Displays the original image with bounding boxes around detected characters and the recognized text with per-character confidences.

- Adds a new section to `README.md` describing these Gradio demos and how to use them.
- Includes a cell in the notebook to install Gradio if not already present.

author: danny0838
body:
This is a revised version of [PR #103033](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/103033), implementing two new methods in `zipfile.ZipFile`: `remove()` and `repack()`, as suggested in [this comment](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/103033#issuecomment-1490705652).

## Features

### `ZipFile.remove(zinfo_or_arcname)`

* Removes a file entry (by providing a `str` path or `ZipInfo`) from the central directory.
* If there are multiple file entries with the same path, only one is removed when a `str` path is provided.
* Returns the removed `ZipInfo` instance.
* Supported in modes: `'a'`, `'w'`, `'x'`.

### `ZipFile.repack(removed=None)`

* Physically removes stale local file entry data that is no longer referenced by the central directory.
* Shrinks the archive file size.
* If `removed` is passed (as a sequence of removed `ZipInfo`s), only their corresponding local file entry data are removed.
* Only supported in mode `'a'`.

## Rationales

### Heuristics Used in `repack()`

Since `repack()` does not immediately clean up removed entries at the time a `remove()` is called, the header information of removed file entries may be missing, and thus it can be technically difficult to determine whether certain stale bytes are really previously removed files and safe to remove.

While local file entries begin with the magic signature `PK\x03\x04`, this alone is not a reliable indicator. For instance, a self-extracting ZIP file may contain executable code before the actual archive, which could coincidentally include such a signature, especially if it embeds ZIP-based content.

To safely reclaim space, `repack()` assumes that in a normal ZIP file, local file entries are **stored consecutively**:
- File entries must not overlap.
  - If any entry’s data overlaps with the next, a `BadZipFile` error is raised and no changes are made.
- There should be no extra bytes between entries (or between the last entry and the central directory):
  1. Data before the first referenced entry is removed only when it appears to be a sequence of consecutive entries with no extra following bytes; extra preceeding bytes are preserved.
  1. Data between referenced entries is removed only when it appears to be a sequence of consecutive entries with no extra preceding bytes; extra following bytes are preserved.

Check the doc in the source code of `_ZipRepacker.repack()` (which is internally called by `ZipFile.repack()`) for more details.

### Supported Modes

There has been opinions that a repacking should support mode `'w'` and `'x'` (e. g. https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/51067#issuecomment-1093479250).

This is **NOT** introduced since such modes do not truncate the file at the end of writing, and won't really shrink the file size after a removal has been made. Although we do can change the behavior for the existing API, some further care has to be made because mode `'w'` and `'x'` may be used on an unseekable file and will be broken by such change. OTOH, mode `'a'` is not expected to work with an unseekable file since an initial seek is made immediately when it is opened.

author: amiralitoori
body:
This script provides functionality to generate a Control Flow Graph (CFG) from Python code and output it in DOT language format.

Key features:
- Parses Python code into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) using the `ast` module.
- Defines `CFGNode` for representing nodes (basic blocks) in the CFG.
- Implements `CFGBuilder` to traverse the AST and construct the CFG.
  - Currently supports sequential statements (assignments, expressions, pass).
  - Includes placeholder visitor methods for control flow statements (If, FunctionDef) which will require further development for correct CFG representation.
- Generates DOT language output for the CFG, allowing visualization with tools like Graphviz.
- A `main` function demonstrates usage with a sample Python script containing sequential statements and an if/else construct. The output shows the current (basic) handling of these structures.
- Includes docstrings and comments for code understanding.

This version lays the groundwork for a more complete CFG generator. Future work will focus on correctly implementing control flow logic.

author: leonidgoltsblat
body:
This PR provides abstraction to pj_barrier_t - synchronization barrier.
It allows threads to block until all participating threads have reached the barrier, ensuring synchronization at specific points in execution. 
pj_barrier_t provides a barrier mechanism for synchronizing threads in a multithreaded application, similar to the POSIX pthread_barrier_wait or Windows EnterSynchronizationBarrier.

This functionality is extracted from #4241 without any changes.

author: doublevv35
body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements to the `EasySave` application, focusing on improving single-instance enforcement, handling of large file transfers, and priority file processing. Additionally, it includes minor refactoring and translation updates for better maintainability and usability.

### Application Behavior Enhancements:
* **Single-Instance Enforcement**: Introduced a `Mutex` in `App.xaml.cs` to ensure only one instance of the application can run at a time. If another instance is detected, the application displays a message and exits. (`[EasySave/EasySave by ProSoft/App.xaml.csR5-R29](diffhunk://#diff-e3b4aa7a859a53fe094f93eebaef8c8868b2c7d69afaed94abfa5270437db86dR5-R29)`)
* **Graceful Mutex Release**: Added an `OnExit` override to release and dispose of the mutex when the application exits. (`[EasySave/EasySave by ProSoft/App.xaml.csR78-R87](diffhunk://#diff-e3b4aa7a859a53fe094f93eebaef8c8868b2c7d69afaed94abfa5270437db86dR78-R87)`)

### Backup Process Improvements:
* **Large File Handling**: Added a new method, `ProcessLargeFileWithSemaphore`, in `BackupJob.cs` to manage large file transfers using a semaphore, ensuring controlled parallelism for large files. (`[EasySave/EasySave by ProSoft/Models/BackupJob.csR454-R481](diffhunk://#diff-378919214ecdffdfb14c320bd9d0dcdbefb8bc644f6a78ade523ba91b1d7ad5dR454-R481)`)
* **Priority File Barrier**: Enhanced the `ProcessFiles` method in `BackupJob.cs` to implement a barrier mechanism that ensures priority files are processed before non-priority files. This includes waiting for all priority files to finish before proceeding with non-priority ones. (`[EasySave/EasySave by ProSoft/Models/BackupJob.csL222-R282](diffhunk://#diff-378919214ecdffdfb14c320bd9d0dcdbefb8bc644f6a78ade523ba91b1d7ad5dL222-R282)`)

### Codebase Refinements:
* **Priority File Check Refactoring**: Replaced the `HasPendingPriorityFiles` method with `HasAnyPendingPriorityFiles` in `BackupManager.cs` for a more efficient and thread-safe implementation using a lock. (`[EasySave/EasySave by ProSoft/Models/BackupManager.csL276-L302](diffhunk://#diff-917539e97949ca7f96b8618bd922e2fdeecdb9bedaa7c0e784c674f4c1fb47e8L276-L302)`)
* **Translation Updates**: Updated debug messages in `App.xaml.cs` to use French, aligning with localized application behavior. (`[EasySave/EasySave by ProSoft/App.xaml.csL29-R66](diffhunk://#diff-e3b4aa7a859a53fe094f93eebaef8c8868b2c7d69afaed94abfa5270437db86dL29-R66)`)

body:
## Changes Made

This PR adds a retry mechanism for handling 429 (Too Many Requests) errors when loading data into Cosmos DB containers. This is particularly important for serverless accounts which have lower throughput limits and are more likely to throttle requests.

### Implementation Details

1. Added a new helper method `CreateItemWithRetryAsync` that:
   - Takes a container and an item as parameters
   - Attempts to create the item using container.CreateItemAsync
   - Catches CosmosException with StatusCode 429 (TooManyRequests)
   - Extracts the "x-ms-retry-after-ms" value from response headers
   - Implements an exponential backoff by waiting for the specified time before retrying
   - Limits the number of retries to prevent infinite loops

2. Updated the `LoadContainerFromFile` method to use this helper:
   - For bulk operations: `concurrentTasks.Add(CreateItemWithRetryAsync(container, record))`
   - For non-bulk operations: `await CreateItemWithRetryAsync(container, record)`

### Benefits

- More resilient data loading process that respects Cosmos DB rate limits
- Intelligent retry behavior based on the server's guidance (x-ms-retry-after-ms header)
- Better handling of serverless account limitations
- Maintains the same overall performance characteristics while adding resiliency

Fixes #40.

body:
## Add Right-Click Action Support to Midscene Framework

### Overview
This MR introduces comprehensive right-click support to the Midscene web automation framework, extending the existing action capabilities to include context menu interactions.

### Changes Made

#### Core Type System
- **`packages/core/src/types.ts`**: Added `PlanningActionParamRightClick` type and updated `PlanningAction` union type to include `'RightClick'`
- **`packages/core/src/index.ts`**: Exported new right-click related types

#### AI Planning & Prompts
- **`packages/core/src/ai-model/prompt/llm-planning.ts`**: Updated AI planning prompts to recognize and handle right-click actions
- **`packages/core/src/yaml.ts`**: Added YAML serialization support for right-click actions

#### Web Integration Layer
- **`packages/web-integration/src/common/plan-builder.ts`**: Extended plan building logic to handle right-click actions
- **`packages/web-integration/src/common/tasks.ts`**: Implemented right-click execution in `PageTaskExecutor`
- **`packages/web-integration/src/common/agent.ts`**: Added public `aiRightClick()` method with the same API pattern as existing actions
- **`packages/web-integration/src/yaml/player.ts`**: Added YAML workflow support for right-click actions

#### API Design
The new right-click functionality follows the established pattern:
```typescript
await agent.aiRightClick("target element description", options?)
```

### Features Implemented
✅ **AI-powered element location**: Right-click uses the same intelligent element detection as other actions  
✅ **YAML workflow support**: Right-click actions can be included in automated workflows  
✅ **Error handling**: Consistent error reporting and execution dump generation  
✅ **Caching support**: Leverages existing task caching mechanisms  
✅ **Multi-platform support**: Works across Puppeteer, Playwright, and Chrome extension backends  

### Testing
Comprehensive test coverage has been added:
- **Unit tests**: Core type validation and plan building logic
- **Integration tests**: End-to-end right-click execution scenarios  
- **YAML workflow tests**: Right-click in automation scripts
- **Cross-platform tests**: Validation across different page implementations

### Validation Steps
To verify this implementation:

1. **Run tests**:
   ```bash
   npm test -- --testNamePattern="rightClick|RightClick"
   ```

2. **Manual testing**:
   ```typescript
   const agent = new PageAgent(page);
   await agent.aiRightClick("button to right click");
   ```

3. **YAML workflow testing**:
   ```yaml
   tasks:
     - name: Right click context menu
       flow:
         - rightClick: "menu trigger button"
   ```

…ation

This commit introduces several new features to integrate AI-powered content generation with a news fetching mechanism.

Key changes include:

- Real AI Service Integration:
    - `aiService.ts` now calls a configurable external AI API for content generation, replacing the previous mock implementation.
- News Fetching Mechanism:
    - Added `newsService.ts` to fetch articles from the GNews API.
    - Introduced a "News Feed" page (`NewsFeed.tsx`) to display these articles.
    - Integrated the News Feed into app routing and sidebar navigation.
- Enhanced Article Generation Workflow:
    - You can now select a news article from the feed to pre-fill the content editor, providing context for AI-assisted writing.
- Configuration Settings:
    - Created a "Settings" page (`Settings.tsx`) where you can configure API keys and endpoints for the AI service (API Key, URL, Model) and the News service (API Key).
    - Settings are persisted in `localStorage` via `configService.ts`.
- Service Updates for Configuration:
    - `aiService.ts` and `newsService.ts` now load their configurations from these settings.
    - `newsService.ts` includes a fallback to mock data if the News API key is not configured, ensuring the News Feed remains browsable.
- Testing:
    - Added unit tests for `configService.ts`, `newsService.ts`, and `aiService.ts` covering core logic, configuration handling, and error scenarios.
    - Outlined a manual testing plan for end-to-end verification.

These features allow you to leverage external news sources and AI capabilities to assist in content creation. The system is designed to be configurable and provides fallbacks for a smoother experience. Full automation and social media distribution were discussed as future backend-dependent enhancements.
